explanation: Entity::update needs the right context type. Views use &mut Context<Self>; the app uses &mut App. You cannot call view methods as if they were free functions on Entity.
fix: Inside impl Render / a listener, use this.field and cx.notify(), or entity.update(cx, |this, cx| { ... }). Do not mix App and Context<T>.

explanation: GPUI has two contexts: App (process-wide) and Context<T> (a view). Window callbacks and Render get Context<Self>. application().run gets App.
fix: In main: |cx: &mut App|. In Render: |cx: &mut Context<Self>|. Use cx.new in both; use cx.notify only on Context<T>.

explanation: render() must return impl IntoElement. div() and most GPUI elements implement it. A raw String works via child(); a custom struct needs impl IntoElement or impl RenderOnce.
fix: Return div()... or wrap content with .child(...). Do not return the view struct itself.

explanation: Window roots created with cx.new(|_| T) must impl Render.
fix: impl Render for T { fn render(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement { ... } }

explanation: Nested entity.update / overlapping &mut Context is a common GPUI pitfall.
fix: Clone the Entity handle, drop the inner borrow, then update. Or cx.defer(|this, cx| ...).

explanation: cx.spawn closures cannot keep &mut Context. Capture Entity (cheap handle) or WeakEntity.
fix: let entity = cx.entity(); cx.spawn(async move |cx| { entity.update(&mut cx, |this, cx| { ... }) }).

explanation: Tailwind-like methods live on the Styled trait (many are macro-generated). The receiver must be a GPUI element such as Div, not a raw struct.
fix: Start from div() (or another element), import gpui::prelude::*, then chain .flex().bg(...). Call gpui_styled_methods for names.

explanation: Foreground vs background executor: not everything is Send. UI types often are not.
fix: Keep GPUI types on the main executor. Use cx.background_spawn only for Send work, then bounce back with cx.spawn / notify.

explanation: Application::new() is stale tutorial API. Current Zed git uses gpui_platform::application().
